intuition.title: Surface termination and island growth
intuition.summary: The authors connect coordinatively saturated, low-energy surfaces with Volmer–Weber three-dimensional nucleation. Tall separated islands at low equivalent coverage support that interpretation. A graphite basal-plane surface energy near 35 dyn/cm is a cited comparison, not a measurement of the present silver / silicon interface.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

general_background.title: Charge transfer at an interface
general_background.summary: Electrochemical conversion couples interfacial charge transfer to chemical change. Transport of reactants and the state of the interface can influence where material forms.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
